assessment: The authors present a study of the swimming behaviour of the zoospores of the water mold Phytophthora (Greek "Plant Destroyer"), which is responsible for significant crop damage worldwide. The motility of the zoospores is likely a significant contributor to the successful spread of the disease, and as such its study has potential wide impact. The authors suggest using a model that the anterior "hairy" (covered with mastigonemes) flagellum is the primary contributor to motility, and show with high-speed imaging that the microorganism is able to turn on the spot by stopping its posterior flagellum, and changing the beat-pattern of its anterior flagellum from "sperm-like" to "Chlamydomonas-like".
